solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Girl with small outhouse, reduced in status

parts.note: a short girl's name, as for Diana
a shed is a small outbuilding

explanation.surface: A girl whose only home is a tiny outhouse has come down in the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone diminished has been lowered or lessened in standing, a straightforward synonym for reduced.

clue.text: Old buccaneer finally turned libertine

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word that follows it

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man

explanation.surface: A pirate of old who ended up living a dissolute life.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan privateer the Spanish regarded as a pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Drake raided Spanish ships and ports for Elizabeth I, so he is a fair example of an old buccaneer.

clue.text: UK citizen, male copper, one visiting granny

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone's home, so one letter goes inside the grandmother word

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
nan is an informal word for a grandmother

explanation.surface: A list of passers-by: a British man, a policeman, someone calling on their grandmother.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a policeman, but here it is the metal. I sits inside NAN after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mancunian is a native or resident of Manchester, so is one particular kind of UK citizen.

clue.text: Declaration of responsibility badly belies one's blog

indicators.note: something done badly comes out in a jumbled, wrong order

parts.note: the letters of these three words, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A blogger's stated sense of duty is undercut by what the blog actually says.
explanation.definitionFit: Noblesse oblige is the principle that privilege brings a duty to act generously, a statement of obligation.

clue.text: Domestic fowl given to a Muslim ruler's wife

parts.note: the Sultan is an ornamental breed of chicken from Turkey

explanation.surface: A farmyard bird is presented as a gift to the consort of an Islamic monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The fowl is not a hen or duck but a chicken breed that happens to share its name with the ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultana is the wife, mother or daughter of a sultan, a Muslim sovereign.

clue.text: One throwing out England's first conqueror

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: a victor is one who conquers

explanation.surface: Someone who expelled England's earliest invader.
explanation.walkthrough: England's first conqueror reads like William the Conqueror; it splits into a letter and a plain synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: An evictor is a person who expels a tenant from a property, i.e. throws them out.

clue.text: American boxer attending Mass in African state

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass
Muhammad Ali, the American heavyweight champion

explanation.surface: Muhammad Ali goes to church while visiting West Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Attending means beside here, so the boxer follows the abbreviation; Mass is the physics quantity, not a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked country in West Africa, so it is an African state.

clue.text: Vestment seen on an early Christian martyr

parts.note: an alb is a white ankle-length vestment worn by clergy

explanation.surface: A clerical garment is spotted on a saint who died for the faith.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, on means placed above, so the vestment sits on top of AN.
explanation.definitionFit: St Alban, executed in Roman Britain, is traditionally counted as Britain's first Christian martyr.

clue.text: Just the same perfect setting for conservationists in charge

indicators.note: a setting surrounds and holds a jewel, so one word encloses the following ones

parts.note: the National Trust, a British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: The ideal location for a team of conservationists who are running things.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust looks after historic houses and countryside in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical means exactly alike, and 'just the same' is the plain phrase for that.

clue.text: Cool chute Tunisians engineered

indicators.note: engineered means built or contrived, so the letters are constructed into something new

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Praise for a slide or ventilation chute built by engineers from Tunisia.
explanation.walkthrough: Cool looks like approval of the chute but is the definition, in its sense of lukewarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A cool reception is a lukewarm one, showing little eagerness or enthusiasm.

clue.text: News welcomed by a murder victim's woman

indicators.note: a guest who is welcomed is taken inside, so the first word goes within the next

parts.note: Abel, killed by his brother Cain in Genesis
N for new, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Reports that a murder victim's female partner has been told the news.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, joining wordplay to definition. NN sits between A and ABEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Annabel is a female first name, so it stands for a woman by example.

clue.text: Contemptible soldier thrown over by peer, perhaps

indicators.note: something thrown over is flipped, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: GI is an American private soldier
a peer is an example of a noble, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: A despicable soldier is tossed aside by an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoble means dishonourable or base, so it describes something deserving contempt.

clue.text: High-spirited former worker sheltering over in Munich

indicators.note: to shelter something is to keep it inside, so one word wraps round another

explanation.surface: A cheerful ex-employee offers someone a place to stay in Bavaria.
explanation.walkthrough: In Munich signals a German word is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Exuberant means full of energy and cheerfulness, a direct synonym for high-spirited.

clue.text: Small group united in Holy Writ

indicators.note: in places one word inside the letters of the next

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, part of Holy Writ

explanation.surface: A little band of people joined together in scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a group of nine musicians, which counts as a small ensemble.

clue.text: Sign of tooth decay displacing top of crown

indicators.note: displacing means moving something out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: caries is the medical term for tooth decay

indicators.note: 'top of' keeps only the first letter of 'crown'

explanation.surface: A symptom of dental rot that has spread to the top of a crown.
explanation.walkthrough: Crown sounds dental, but only its first letter is wanted, which is then removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the ram, is the first sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Traveller crossing river in a Spanish-speaking country

indicators.note: crossing means spanning across, so one word lies over another and takes it inside

parts.note: a commercial traveller is a sales agent
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A traveller fording a stream somewhere in Latin America.
explanation.walkthrough: A commercial traveller is an old term for a salesman on the road, hence agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a South American country whose official language is Spanish.

clue.text: Like several religions mentioned at first in revised Bach aria

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so the letters are rearranged
at first asks for the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Several faiths get a mention early on in a reworked Bach aria.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter goes in among the Bach aria letters before the whole lot is mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Judaism, Christianity and Islam are called the Abrahamic religions because they trace descent from Abraham.

clue.text: Chew acorns, say, consumed after mince regularly

indicators.note: after says the word before it is placed second, behind the piece from the words that follow

parts.note: mast is the fallen nuts of forest trees, such as acorns and beech nuts

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of mince

explanation.surface: An instruction to munch acorns, eaten once you have finished the mince.
explanation.walkthrough: Mast is the forest-floor crop of nuts that pigs were turned out to eat; acorns, say marks acorns as an example of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To masticate is to grind food with the teeth, the formal word for chewing.

clue.text: Boatman, one with no future outside lido, sadly

indicators.note: outside means one word wraps round the other
sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters come out disordered

explanation.surface: A doomed boatman stranded outside a public swimming pool, a sorry sight.
explanation.walkthrough: A lido is an open-air swimming pool, and the Venice Lido is near gondola country.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondolier rows a gondola on Venice's canals, so is a kind of boatman.

clue.text: Pander to popular Law Lord going over notes

indicators.note: going over suggests turning around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: lud, as in m'lud, is how a judge is addressed
two musical notes, G and E

explanation.surface: Currying favour with a fashionable senior judge as he reads through his notes.
explanation.walkthrough: Over also places the turned word above the notes in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To indulge someone is to gratify their wishes, the same as pandering to them.

clue.text: State of Arab entering Burlington House

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so one word sits within another

parts.note: the Royal Academy of Arts has its home at Burlington House in London
a native of Oman is an Arab

explanation.surface: The condition of an Arab visitor walking into a London gallery building.
explanation.walkthrough: Burlington House on Piccadilly houses the Royal Academy, giving RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Romania is a country in south-east Europe, so it is a state.

clue.text: Fibre in vegetableS IS A Luxury

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: spans the end of the first word to the start of the last

explanation.surface: Dietary fibre in vegetables is a luxury.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a stiff plant fibre from an agave, used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Month the Spanish must produce literary work

explanation.surface: A month's deadline for the Spaniards to write a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A novel is a book-length piece of prose fiction, a type of literary work.

clue.text: Farewell ultimately apt for a gentleman's gentleman

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the closing letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye in the end is fitting for a gentleman's personal servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentleman's gentleman is the traditional phrase for a valet, a man's personal manservant.

clue.text: Fuming about tribe's consignment to hellfire

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a nation can be a tribe or people

explanation.surface: Someone livid about a tribe being condemned to the fires of hell.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation is condemnation to eternal punishment in hell.

clue.text: Impoverished woman brought up in US city

indicators.note: in places one word inside another
brought up means raised, and in a down clue a raised word reads from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A poor woman raised in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Needy means lacking money and necessities, a synonym for impoverished.

clue.text: Banned drug swallowed by sick young woman

indicators.note: swallowed means taken inside, so one item goes within another

parts.note: gal is informal for a girl

explanation.surface: A sick young woman has taken a prohibited drug.
explanation.walkthrough: E for ecstasy is a standard crossword abbreviation; gal is a casual American-flavoured word for a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Something banned is forbidden by law, which is what illegal means.

clue.text: Reported out-of-hours charge for fertiliser, perhaps

indicators.note: reported means said aloud, so the answer sounds like the phrase

parts.note: a night rate is a charge made for work out of normal hours

explanation.surface: A tradesman reports what he charges after hours for supplying fertiliser.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrates such as ammonium nitrate are widely used as fertilisers, hence perhaps.

clue.text: Culturally pretentious leader leaving political group

indicators.note: the leader is the front letter, and leaving says it departs

explanation.surface: A pretentious leader quits his political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty describes someone showily claiming interest in the arts, i.e. pretentiously cultured.

clue.text: Lewdness of French composer transfixed by posh English trains

indicators.note: transfixed means pierced through, so one letter is driven into the middle of a word

parts.note: RY, railway, the system that runs trains

explanation.surface: The debauchery of a French composer who loves posh English trains.
explanation.walkthrough: Of French reads like part of the definition but gives the French word. U for upper-class is a long-standing British label.
explanation.definitionFit: Debauchery is indulgence in sensual pleasures, which covers lewd behaviour.
